prompt:
Task packet (meal-planner, ~/Workspace/meal-planner). Bug: a two-page NYT recipe PDF (Old-Fashioned Beef Stew) parses wrong. In pdf-parse's reading order, page 1 ends mid-ingredient ('1 medium onion, peeled and' then the PREPARATION steps and the recipe's description paragraph), and page 2 starts with the ingredient overflow ('chopped', then three more ingredients) before the rest of the last step.
- `parsePdfText(text)` in `lib/parser.ts` must keep all 12 ingredients, with no duplicates: the continuation joins its ingredient across the page break (`medium onion, peeled and chopped`), the overflow ingredients after the break are ingredients (carrots, potatoes, `salt` exactly once), and the parser must not repeat the last ingredient.
- The instructions resume after the overflow ingredients and end with `Ladle among 4 bowls and serve.`; the description paragraph ('This classic stick-to-your-ribs stew ...') is not part of the steps.
Done when `node scripts/test-parser.mjs` reports `0/N parser checks failed`. Keep existing tests' assertions as they are.

expect: (?m)^PASS beef\ stew\ retains\ all\ 12\ ingredients\ without\ duplication$
(?m)^PASS beef\ stew\ retains\ every\ ingredient\ name$
(?m)^PASS beef\ stew\ onion\ continuation\ survives\ the\ page\ break$
(?m)^PASS beef\ stew\ overflow\ does\ not\ duplicate\ its\ last\ ingredient$
(?m)^PASS beef\ stew\ final\ step\ resumes\ after\ overflow\ ingredients$

mined.subject: Handle Beef Stew PDF overflow layout
